newsitem.title: JAPAN: EU urges Japan to map out bold deregulation.
newsitem.headline: EU urges Japan to map out bold deregulation.

text.p: The European Union urged Japan to carry out bold deregulation measures, especially in the area of distribution, when it draws up a final reform programme by the end of March, a senior EU official told reporters on Thursday.

"It is time for the Japanese government to take the bit between their teeth, take all their courage and take a decisive step forward in this process," said Gerard Depayre, Deputy Director-General for External Relations in the European Commission.
Depayre is in Tokyo this week to attend high level meeting on deregulation between Japan and EU officials.

He said Japan's interim report for a three-year deregulation programme issued in January, to be finalised by the end of March, did not go far enough in opening of the Japanese market in areas which the EU had an interest.
"We have very mixed, not to say, disappointing assessment," he said, but added that progress in some areas such as cars, asset management and telecommunication was indisputable.
The areas which had limited or no progress were distribution, sanitary issues, standards and testing of industrial products as well as agriculture and health-related issues, Depayre said.
The EU urged Japan to ensure a change in anticompetitive business practices and give retailers freedom to choose suppliers, products and prices.

It also urged Japan to make substantial amendment of the Large Scale Retail Store Law by 1997 so that competitors in the sector will not be able to hinder or delay the opening or enlargement of a store.
